Confirmed. The Stop hook's flagged mutations produced **no uncommitted durable ledger change**:

- Both my authored source files are hash-identical at HEAD and on disk (`3cb40062…`, `a595a597…`), and all three of my commits are ancestors of HEAD.
- My only post-commit file mutations were the two **memory files** (`MEMORY.md` and `laurent-ring-case-scheme-bridge.md`), which live *outside* the workspace ledger, plus an `inbox read` state change — none of these are ledger source.
- The `D` (staged-deletion) entries in the shared index are the documented I-1222 hazard: files present at both HEAD and disk, staged-deleted by workspace churn, **not authored by me**. I committed exclusively through fresh private indices (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`), never the shared one, so I introduced none of them, and I am not running any plain commit that would realize them.

There is nothing of mine left to commit. My work is complete and durable. Session done — final report stands as written above.
